data.exact_reserve_text: The result is driven by reserve increases in the closed years, where the 2013 and 2016 years have required reserve strengthening beyond their respective pure year close position. In contrast the 2014 and 2015 years are performing better than expected when those years were closed. Unfavourable development for 2016 is particularly disappointing and is driven by catastrophe losses, strengthening of liability reserves and a deterioration in Specialty loss ratios. The loss for the year has been impacted by movements in the 2017 and prior year accounts, coupled with the effect of tornado losses attaching to the 2018 year of account. The result for the account has been impacted by the movement in large claim reserves for the 2013 and 2014 years, and late development of certain claims from the 2015 year, as well as an adjustment to reserves on certain more specialised business. For the 2016 year, catastrophe losses, liability reserve increases and Specialty class loss ratio deterioration have specifically contributed to the loss. The 2017 pure year of account has delivered a profit at the three year stage.

data.standardized_narrative: During 2019, the syndicate experienced mixed prior year development, resulting in a net release of GBP 3.732 million. This was driven by reserve strengthening for the 2013 and 2016 underwriting years, with the 2016 year particularly impacted by catastrophe losses, strengthening of liability reserves, and deterioration in Specialty loss ratios. Conversely, the 2014, 2015, and 2017 underwriting years performed better than expected, contributing to releases. Specific factors included movements in large claim reserves for 2013 and 2014, late development of claims for 2015, and adjustments to reserves on more specialised business.
